root_idea.summary: The root centers on breaking or crushing something, whether hollow or non-hollow.
root_idea.development: Its lexical development includes crushing objects such as bone and bread, the state of dry vegetation broken into pieces, a head wound that breaks bone, and specialized extensions for milking an udder and showing compassion.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under the normalized citation form هَشِيم.

senses.definition: Dry, brittle plant matter broken into pieces; dry vegetation reduced to fragments.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it describes vegetation in a dried and broken state, including imagery of wind-scattered stalks or twig-like fragments.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form I verb; the lexical evidence applies it, among other things, to crushing a bone or bread.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To crush or break something thoroughly, into many pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II verb described with dry things and hollow objects, including the head; these examples illustrate the intensified action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become dry and broken into pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V verb used of a plant or herbage becoming هَشِيم.
A Classical adjectival use describing a person as physically weak.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A head wound that breaks the skull bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a wound or blow causing fracture of the head bone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To milk all that is in a she-camel’s udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form VIII usage concerning extracting the milk from the udder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show compassion or take pity on someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction of the form تَهَشَّمَ فُلَانٌ عَلَى فُلَانٍ, “he showed compassion toward him.”

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Form I meaning “to crush” is represented.
The intensified Form II crushing meaning is represented.
The Form V sense of becoming dry and broken is represented.
The noun’s dry, broken-vegetation meaning is represented in the Quranic form.
The specialized head-wound meaning is represented.
Pointer-only cross-reference to كُرٌّ; it supplies no independent lexical definition.

cautions: The Quranic translations “dry stalks” and “dry twig fragments” illustrate the same lexical sense of هَشِيم rather than separate meanings.
